rv.q: Rob McClure as Charlie Chaplin in " Chaplin the Musical" (Joan Marcus) Credit: Rob McClure as Charlie Chaplin in " Chaplin the Musical" (Joan Marcus) You've probably seen worse musicals than "Chaplin," a forgettable biography of Charlie Chaplin.
As a musical, Chaplin is squarely in the middle of the middle of the pack; as the canny redeployment of an icon, it sometimes flirts with excellence.

Charles Chaplin had an amazing first act—a rags-to-riches tale of artistic triumph—and a crummy second one—personal scandal, political exile, and after The Great Dictator, a string of mediocre talkies.

Too bad that that his strong efforts aren't better supported in this mostly uninspired effort, featuring a largely unmemorable score by Christopher Curtis and a schematic, psychology-heavy book by Curtis and Thomas Meehan (Annie, The Producers).
But they have come up all thumbs, alas, in the writing and staging departments.
Despite an enigmatic, career-making performance from Rob McClure in the title role... 'Chaplin' is a musical where the material is just not up to the complexity of its enigmatic subject.
The show McClure leads is equal parts flat, overwrought and tiresome.
This may be a mercy, given the lines he has to say.

The problem with 'Chaplin' is that it tries to cram too much of the comedian's long, eventful life into a single evening, with the result that it feels more like a highlight reel than a fully realized dramatic experience.
It’s not a great sign when you leave a musical thinking more about the visuals than the songs — which is exactly what happens at Broadway’s new “Chaplin.”
In the new musical Chaplin, which is every bit as entertaining as Charlie Chaplin himself
Rob McClure gives a winning performance as the Little Tramp in this biographical musical that hits more often than it misses.
The way "Chaplin" stands now, it's modestly entertaining.
If only to enjoy the trajectory of this unique artist, you should see “Chaplin.”
Their show too often plays like a silent movie dubbed over with the wrong soundtrack.

cn.t: Critics find "Chaplin" a mediocre biomusical saved by Rob McClure's star-making performance, but hampered by forgettable songs, overly sentimental storytelling, and a PowerPoint-like rush through the icon's life story.
